title: Fan Power and Efficiency Calculator
description: Three challenges that ask for brake horsepower or static efficiency from airflow, fan static pressure and one other quantity, followed by free exploration of airflow, pressure and efficiency with live air power and BHP readouts and power bars.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: brake horsepower
fan efficiency
air power
fan static pressure
fan performance
rights: Copyright 2026 Twin City Fan. All rights reserved.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate a fan's brake horsepower or static efficiency from its airflow volume, fan static pressure and one of the other two quantities, to within 2% of the model value.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts, each new challenge and the end-of-challenge summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; the losses part of the BHP bar is hatched as well as coloured; Enter checks and goes to the next challenge; every button, the answer box and the sliders are reachable with Tab.

controls.label: Your answer
controls.purpose: Type the BHP (challenges 1-2) or static efficiency in percent (challenge 3)

controls.label: Check
controls.purpose: Check the answer (Enter); 2% tolerance, two attempts

controls.label: Next challenge / Start exploring
controls.purpose: Advance after a challenge is resolved (Enter)

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Reset the three challenges and the score

equations: Static efficiency (%) = 100 x air power / BHP
rules: Model answers rounded to two decimals for hp and one decimal for percent
Correct when |answer - model| / model <= 0.02; two attempts per challenge
A blank or non-numeric answer is not graded; the learner is asked to enter a number
An answer about 100 times too small adds a reminder to enter efficiency as a decimal (challenges 1-2) or in percent (challenge 3)
assumptions: US fan units: CFM, in. wg, horsepower
BHP is shaft power before belt, sheave and motor losses
limitations: Challenge duties are illustrative, not catalog ratings

sources: Equations and the constant 6,356: standard US-unit fan engineering (Chapter 10, 'Brake Horsepower and Fan Efficiency')
Challenge duties: illustrative; challenge 1 matches the chapter's worked example

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Practice with check (commit a number before the model value is revealed), then guided exploration
keyQuestions: Why is BHP always larger than air power?
How much more power does the same duty need at 50% static efficiency than at 70%?
commonMisconceptions: Efficiency entered as a whole number (70 instead of 0.70)
A less efficient fan needs less power because it does less work
assessmentOpportunities: Running score shown as 'Challenges correct: n of 3'; mastery is 3 of 3 within 2% of the model value on the first attempt.
